Definition: Percentage of the national population covered by at least one 4G/LTE mobile network signal, whether or not they subscribe to the service. 4G is the practical minimum for meaningful broadband connectivity enabling digital services.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The cited figure (91.4-93.5% of connections classified 3G/4G/5G-capable) measures the technology mix of connections, not population coverage, so it does not directly support a population-coverage score. A second source (World Bank/GSMA-derived Digital Development diagnostic) records 3G population coverage of ~77% but shows 0% for 4G specifically, which conflicts with confirmed commercial LTE operation by both national operators. No authoritative GSMA/ITU 4G population-coverage percentage was found. Human review needed; recommend sourcing ARME's 2025 mobile coverage/quality field-test report (consumidor.arme.cv), which tested 2G/3G/4G coverage directly.

Definition: Affordability of mobile broadband data, measured as the cost of a basic mobile data plan (1-2GB) as a percentage of GNI per capita. The UN Broadband Commission target is below 2% of monthly GNI per capita. Affordability is the single largest barrier to internet adoption in Africa.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The cited A4AI 2017 table does not actually list Cape Verde, so the original source does not support the score. Fresher data conflicts: Cable.co.uk/Statista (2023) puts average 1GB at USD3.24 (cheapest USD1.62), which against 2023 GNI p.c. of USD4,740 (World Bank) is roughly 0.4-0.8% of monthly income; but a separate diagnostic (digitaldevelopment.org) records a USD5.02 basket (~1.3% of GNI), and Research ICT Africa's Q4 2025 RAMP index explicitly flags Cabo Verde, alongside Seychelles and Comoros, as structurally high-priced due to island/undersea-cable costs. Estimates straddle the boundary between 'Affordable (1-2%)' and 'Meets UN target (<1%)'; flagged for human review rather than reclassified on conflicting figures.

Determined by submarine cable landings (for coastal states), cross-border terrestrial fibre (for landlocked states), and satellite links.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The ITU figure (12.33 kbit/s per user, 2016) is confirmed as reported but is nearly a decade old, and a second diagnostic (digitaldevelopment.org) shows international bandwidth per user of 23.36 in an unclear year/unit, which would fall in the 'Moderate (20-49 kbit/s)' band. No current, unambiguous ITU or TeleGeography figure was found. Human review recommended to resolve the conflicting figures and source a post-2020 estimate given new submarine cable landings referenced in African Business (2025).

Definition: Whether the country has an operational Internet Exchange Point (IXP) and its maturity. IXPs enable local internet traffic to be exchanged domestically rather than being routed internationally, reducing latency, costs, and dependence on foreign infrastructure. Critical for local digital ecosystem development.
Comments: CVIXP active public IXP in Praia [Data Center Map](https://www.datacentermap.com/ixp/cabo-verde-internet-exchange-point/)
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: PeeringDB (fetched directly) confirms CV-IXP is operational in Praia but records only 5 peers, 6 connections and 23G total capacity, with one peer on a selective (non-open) policy. This is a single IXP with limited participation rather than moderate participation, so the code is revised down from 4 to 3 ('Single IXP with limited participation').

Definition: Unique mobile subscriber penetration rate as a percentage of the total population. Measures the proportion of individuals who subscribe to a mobile service (not SIM cards, which can be multiple per person). Mobile phones are the primary device for internet access in Africa.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The cited figure is SIM/connection penetration (114-115%, confirmed by national regulator ARME via Telecompaper, Dec 2025), not GSMA's unique-subscriber metric that this variable specifically requires. However, Cabo Verde's market has only two operators and a modest SIM 'excess' (112-115% of population), implying comparatively low multi-SIM ownership; combined with internet usage of ~74%, unique subscriber penetration is very likely still above 70% of population. Value Code 5 confirmed on this basis, though the underlying source metric mismatch (SIMs vs unique subscribers) should be corrected in future collection.

Definition: The availability and presence of major cloud service providers (hyperscale and regional) operating in or serving the country with local or near-local infrastructure. Cloud availability determines access to scalable computing resources for government, business, and startups.
Value Name: Regional cloud availability zone nearby (same sub-region)
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The cited source discusses only the government's own NOSi cloud (not commercial hyperscale providers), so it does not actually support a claim of nearby regional hyperscale availability. Verified AWS/Azure/GCP infrastructure maps show the nearest availability zones are in South Africa (Cape Town/Johannesburg) — a different African sub-region roughly 5,000km from Cabo Verde — with no confirmed hyperscale presence in West Africa or the Atlantic islands. Revised down to 2 ('Served remotely from distant regions only') given no evidence of a same-sub-region hyperscale zone; the original score conflated a domestic government cloud with commercial cloud availability.

Definition: Whether the country has established policies, regulations, and programmes supporting off-grid and distributed energy solutions (mini-grids, solar home systems). These are critical for extending ICT infrastructure to unserved areas beyond the central grid.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The 2017 source is a decade-old aspirational article about grid-connected wind/solar targets, not off-grid policy specifically. Fresher evidence shows a mature, active regulatory and delivery framework: Decree-Law 54/2018 and Law 52/X/2025 provide licensing/network-access rules for independent mini-/medium-scale and microgeneration producers; the government signed four new micro-grid contracts (April 2025) for isolated communities on Santo Antão, São Nicolau and Fogo; and ECREEE/USAID inaugurated a solar mini-grid at Chã das Caldeiras, Fogo (2024). This is a comprehensive legal framework with active, multi-island deployment, so the code is revised up from 3 to 4 ('Comprehensive framework with significant deployment').

redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed directly against the primary source: the UN EGDI database (EGOVKB) and the UN E-Government Survey 2024 Chapter 3 both give Cabo Verde an EGDI of 0.6238 (rank 111 globally, Western Africa region). Value Code 3 confirmed, and the citation is upgraded from the secondary Ecofin article (which did not itself state the EGDI figure) to the primary UN source.

Comments: Moderate ICT education programs, TechPark training [LBC](https://lbc-global.com/en/transformacao-do-ensino-em-cabo-verde-via-as-tic/)

revision_notes: The cited source is entirely mismatched: it describes a 2016 primary/secondary school ICT programme (Mundu Novu), not tertiary ICT/STEM education. Direct verification of Cabo Verde's higher-education offer finds only two institutions with confirmed ICT/computer-engineering degree programmes: the public Universidade de Cabo Verde (Bachelor's and Master's in Engenharia Informática e de Computadores, plus Engenharia Eletrotécnica e de Computadores) and the private Universidade Lusófona de Cabo Verde (Engenharia Informática de Computadores). With only two identified institutions rather than 'several', the code is revised down from 3 to 2 ('Limited: few institutions, low enrolment').
